roles.title: Senior C++ Developer - Vice President
roles.eligibility: No graduation-year or student gate. No stated years-of-experience minimum; VP title implies senior hire. Visa language on posting: 'We can only employ [overseas workers from outside the EEA] if we can provide evidence that there are no other suitable candidates for this vacancy from inside the EEA.'
roles.requirements: Proven C/C++ development experience | Order entry gateway development | Linux | Network protocols (beneficial) | Kernel development experience (beneficial) | FPGA understanding useful; scripting; agile team environment
roles.notes: Team is Latency Sensitive Electronic Trading (LSET), listed under Group Technology - the single best track fit at Nomura for this candidate (low-latency C++, kernel/FPGA adjacency). Listed division on the search page is Group Technology. VP is a stretch title for ~18 months experience; the posting states no minimum, but expect a senior bar. UK HPI visa is self-sponsored so the EEA-resident-labour-market wording above is not a blocker in practice, but the posting's wording is stale/legacy.

roles.title: Credit Quantitative Research - Associate/Vice President
roles.eligibility: No graduation-year gate. Requires 'first-class degree from a top-tier university in Mathematics, Theoretical Physics or similar quantitative field'. Financial-maths/derivatives experience listed as desirable, not required.
roles.requirements: Model development and implementation for Structured Credit Derivatives and XVA | Analytics work spanning Regulatory Capital and Initial Margin | Work with Trading, Structuring and Risk Management | First-class quantitative degree from a top-tier university | Financial mathematics / derivatives knowledge desirable | Strong written and oral communication
roles.notes: Global Markets division, front-office quant (strats) rather than model validation. This is derivatives pricing quant work - stochastic calculus and XVA, not ML/statistical alpha research. Associate band is the realistic entry point for this candidate's experience level.

roles.title: eTrading Developer (Fixed Income)
roles.eligibility: No graduation-year or student gate; no explicit years-of-experience minimum stated. Posting says Nomura can consider overseas applicants needing a UK Tier 2 / Skilled Worker visa only 'if we can provide evidence that this is a genuine vacancy for a qualified role'.
roles.requirements: Degree in Computer Science, Mathematics, Physics or related quantitative field | Strong C++, Java or Python in low-latency environments | Deep understanding of market microstructure, order types and exchange connectivity | Design/optimise execution algorithms and price prediction models | Statistical analysis and machine learning proficiency | Preferred: market making, KDB, MiFID II familiarity, distributed systems
roles.notes: Hybrid quant-dev / strat role sitting in Global Markets (not Group Technology) - closest thing Nomura London has to a systematic-trading strat seat. Blends C++ low-latency work with ML price prediction, so it also reads on the Research track. HPI visa removes the sponsorship friction the posting describes.

roles.title: Algo Developer - Associate / Vice President
roles.eligibility: No graduation-year gate. 'Bachelor or Master degree in computer science, engineering or related disciplines'. Tier 2 Skilled Worker sponsorship language present on the posting.
roles.requirements: Design and development experience with algorithmic trading systems in equity markets | Hands-on Java coding for algo trading systems (essential) | Full project lifecycle: analysis, design, development, testing | Level 2/3 support for front-office applications | Preferred: CI/CD, distributed and event-driven message-oriented architecture, TCP/IP and enterprise messaging
roles.notes: Global Execution Services (Wholesale IT). Caveat: the essential language stack is Java, not C++ - filed under the C++/trading-systems track because the domain is equity algo trading infrastructure, but this candidate's C++/GPU evidence is only partially transferable. Permanent role.

roles.title: Algo Developer - 6 to 12 month contract
roles.eligibility: Fixed-term 6-12 month contract. 'Bachelor or Master degree in computer science, engineering or related disciplines'. No graduation-year gate.
roles.requirements: Hands-on experience coding and developing algorithmic trading systems in Java | Deliver features, enhancements and bug fixes to the algo trading platform | Full project lifecycle involvement | Adherence to functional architecture strategy and development standards | Occasional level 2/3 front-office support
roles.notes: Same Global Execution Services team and near-identical spec to the permanent Algo Developer req above - apply to the permanent one instead unless a contract suits. Contract length clears the >6-month scope bar but a fixed term is a weak fit for someone relocating. Java-first, not C++.

roles.title: Vice President, Electronic FX Full Stack Strategist
roles.eligibility: Not determinable - see notes. VP title implies a senior hire.
roles.requirements: Not retrievable - the job-detail body did not render; the page served only title, location (Singapore), division (Global Markets) and job code 11850 with an Apply button
roles.notes: Title and live status confirmed on Nomura's own portal, but the description body would not load for me, so requirements are unknown - do not assume. On title alone this is the strongest systematic/e-trading strat seat in Nomura's Asia book (eFX pricing/quoting stack, typically C++ or Java plus Python research). Req ID is comparatively old, so it may be a long-running or evergreen posting. Singapore needs sponsorship for this candidate; routine at VP level, but note Nomura's own Asia early-careers FAQ says Singapore programs require citizens/PRs - that restriction is stated for internships/graduate programs, not experienced hires.

roles.title: FX Strategist
roles.eligibility: Postgraduate degree in Finance, Economics or related. Minimum 3 years FX strategy experience in financial services and minimum 2 years covering FX research in Southeast Asian markets - this candidate does not meet either gate.
roles.requirements: Develop and drive FX strategy across Southeast Asia (Singapore, Indonesia, Thailand, Philippines, India) | Produce institutional client research and trade ideas | Basic programming (R/Python/Matlab) to analyse market data | Proven track record publishing market commentary and strategy reports | Excellent written and verbal communication
roles.notes: Sell-side macro research, not systematic/quant research - the coding bar is 'basic R/Python'. Poor fit for this candidate's profile and gated on 3 years of published FX strategy. Listed for completeness of the Research track only.

roles.title: VP, Equity Specialist (Night Trader)
roles.eligibility: 'Minimum 3 years of experience in equity trading or dealing within a financial institution' and a valid MAS Capital Markets Services (CMS) licence for securities dealing - this candidate meets neither.
roles.requirements: Valid MAS Capital Markets Services (CMS) licence for securities dealing | Minimum 3 years equity trading/dealing experience | Bachelor's in Finance or Economics minimum | Bloomberg Terminal / Reuters Eikon or similar market data systems | Willingness to work night shifts | Strong analytical and communication skills
roles.notes: International Wealth Management, not Global Markets - this is client execution/dealing on a night desk, not systematic or prop trading. Licence requirement is a hard gate. Included because it is the only role on the Trader track live in an in-scope location, but it is not a realistic target.

roles.title: Associate, AI Engineer (Singapore)
roles.eligibility: 'Minimum 5 years relevant experience in data engineering, GenAI or full-stack engineering'; Bachelor's (4-year) in a quantitative field or Master's in CS/Engineering/Statistics. The 5-year minimum is a gate this candidate does not clear.
roles.requirements: LLMs, prompt engineering, RAG and agentic systems | Context-aware multi-turn dialogue systems | API/SDK development for GenAI integration; microservices and server-side APIs | Python, SQL, Unix scripting | Cloud (AWS EC2, EMR or equivalent); CI/CD via Jenkins/GitLab | React UI development preferred
roles.notes: Group Technology / International AI CoE. This is LLM application engineering (RAG, agents, Python services), NOT GPU/kernel/ML-performance work - the candidate's llama.cpp kernel background is only tangentially relevant and the role is a level down from research engineering. A VP-band 'Vice President, AI Engineer (Singapore)' (req 1345754900) and an 'Associate, AI Data Scientist (Singapore)' (req 1369436100) are live in the same team; I did not read those two bodies, so treat their requirements as unverified.

existing_rows_audit.detail: Nomura's Tokyo office plainly exists (global HQ), but no such req is findable: careers.nomura.com returns 'There are currently no open positions matching Tokyo' (https://careers.nomura.com/Nomura/search/?q=&locationsearch=Tokyo) because Japan hiring runs on a separate domestic site, and that site's mid-career requirements page states 現在、情報の掲載はございません - 'currently no information posted' (https://www.nomura-recruit.jp/career/requirements/). The row's existing 'Reported' verification status was correct; there is no live Tokyo Quant Developer posting to confirm the title, the ¥8-13M band or the Japanese-language gate. Treat every field on that row as unverified rather than confirmed.

notes: Primary source throughout was Nomura's own SAP SuccessFactors portal at careers.nomura.com, which covers Nomura globally EXCEPT Japan. I enumerated by location filter rather than keyword: London returned exactly 50 live reqs (startrow=50 returned an empty page, so 50 is the complete set), Singapore 35, Hong Kong 20, Frankfurt 7-8, Paris 5. Shanghai and Milan returned 'no open positions' - that means no live reqs, NOT that the office is absent, and I could not verify the office list because nomuraholdings.com returned HTTP 403 to me. The same 403 caveat applies to Amsterdam, Dublin and Warsaw: I found no listings and no confirmed office, so they are recorded as not-found rather than non-existent. Hong Kong has 20 live reqs but ZERO in any of the four tracks - the closest are Global Markets risk/control and compliance roles, so Hong Kong contributes nothing. Frankfurt and Paris are similarly all HR, Finance, Risk, Compliance and Legal - no quant, dev or trading reqs at all. London is where essentially all of Nomura's in-scope hiring sits. An older London req, 'Algorithmic Trading Model Risk Quantitative Analyst (Associate)' (req 1326839900), surfaced in web search but is NOT in the current 50-item London listing, so I treat it as closed and did not include it; it was model validation rather than front-office quant in any case. One London posting I deliberately excluded: 'Software Engineer (Associate) - GMIT Trade Processing' (Group Technology) - post-trade processing infrastructure, outside all four tracks. Same for 'Senior Java Developer' (Group Technology, generic). Overall read: Nomura is a bank, not a quant shop; the only two reqs a systematic/low-latency candidate should genuinely target are the London Senior C++ Developer (LSET) and the London eTrading Developer (Fixed Income). No compensation figures were stated on any posting I opened, so every comp_local field is deliberately empty - nothing was extrapolated.
